pass_a_gloss: ...they guard us. Ch. 40, 5. Who set the measures of it, if you know? Or who brought the measuring rod upon it? They indeed wished to say something Greek about the measure of the earth; the diameter of the earth, they say, is twenty-five myriads of stadia. It seems, however, that the Word shows that the measure of the earth is incomprehensible to all; but only the Savior knew it, He who is also the Creator. And He said 'measures', and not 'a measure', in order that he might represent the differences of the earth. What is the measure of such a thing, tell me, of that which carries the garments of the East? The measure of that which carries the pepper or the animals? For not all things happen everywhere; therefore these are the measures according to the Word of God. – So not simply has the earth become such a size, nor as it happened by chance, but it seems to me, even if the accidental were added, to be unseasonable, and if it were removed, to be like the whole of it being destroyed according to the Word; and this is hinted at by the measures and the rod. ʹ. And who is the one who cast a cornerstone upon it? And who is the one who cast a cornerstone upon it, so that thus it stands firmly, as if having built upon a secure foundation of establishment; by the counsel of God, for in His hand are all the borders of the earth. – A cornerstone; this can also be understood as referring to the Only-begotten Son of God, having been made flesh through us; according to that in the Psalms: A stone, which they rejected, became the head of a corner. For having come upon the earth in the favor of the Father, He joined in Himself the two peoples, both the Jews and the Gentiles, just as also the cornerstone joins both the walls. 14. And I said to her: Until this, it shall flow, and it shall not exceed. And the Ally: May the limit of your waves be commanded thus. For indeed it holds it safely as if with bars; but also easily, as if by order. For I said, he says, and it is not possible to oppose, when, with no necessity pushing, this happens; even while much of the force and the strength is whipping it; for this reason He did not allow it to be calm, nor peaceful, so that it might proclaim the strength of God, fighting against nature by the command, and conquering everywhere the command. For if the water were peaceful, the order of the nature of water... if many were reckoned; but now the [things] being beaten, scourged, pushed within, and being unable to exceed the boundaries, through the disturbance proclaims the power of God. [Chapter] 28, 27. But what prepared the raven for food? For it is said that it does not nourish its young; but they themselves, although being great, provide food in a certain way. And the young, who nourishes them? Is it not the Word of God? Just as also the Gospel says: The birds of the heaven do not sow, nor do they reap, and your Father the heavenly feeds them. [Chapter] 28, 27. Upon which command of yours is the eagle raised? And the vulture, having settled upon his carcass, howls on a high rock and in secret? ...If in the carnivores there is any logical wisdom, from the knowledge according to nature being present to each, and towards knowledge, to the one whom I call, to the ones of the dead, you see even one carrying a vulture. [Chapter] 24. Why am I still being judged, being admonished and reproving the Lord, hearing such things, being nothing? Why still, he says, am I being judged, for my future? And from the beginning he withdrew from the first things. I am defeated, he says, before you in the just matter; why do you bring the judgment forward more boldly? For what is possible to answer? And how is it necessary to face such a master? I, he says, was continuing, seeking the cause of the plague which happened upon me; but for a creation I summoned no one, and towards the things having been said I have nothing to say. —He leaves, as if not even reproving the Lord, being admonished, the wretched man. [Chapter] 4, 4. But to live, just as a man, [by] your strength, and I will ask you, and you answer me. For those who are possessed of rights, not fleeing the adversaries, they release, so that from possession, the victory might become. Then he also defends himself, that it matters to me concerning men; it is clear from there, for whom exactly this brought the temptation upon you. I give you boldness, I will ask you, and you answer me. [Chapter] 3. He thinks indeed that I have used you otherwise, except that you might appear just? pass_b_english: They stand as our guardians. (Ch. 40, 5) If you have any knowledge, tell me: who established the earth's dimensions? Or who applied the measuring rod to it? Some have attempted to offer a secular explanation regarding the earth's scale, claiming its diameter spans twenty-five myriads of stadia. Yet the Word reveals that the earth's true measure remains beyond all human comprehension; only the Savior, who is also the Creator, possesses this knowledge. He spoke of 'measures' in the plural rather than a single 'measure' to illustrate the diverse variations found across the earth. Tell me, what could be the measure of that which carries the fragrances of the East? What is the measure of that which carries the spices or the living creatures? Since not all things are found in every place, these dimensions are determined by the Word of God. The earth has not simply reached this size by chance or through random occurrence. It seems to me that even if accidental elements were included, they would be out of place; conversely, if they were removed, the entire structure would be ruined according to the divine logic. The mention of measures and the rod alludes to this.

Who is it that has laid the cornerstone upon the earth? Who has set this cornerstone so that the world stands so firmly, as if built upon a secure and established foundation? It is by the counsel of God, for all the boundaries of the earth are held in His hand. This cornerstone can be understood as a reference to the Only-begotten Son of God, who became flesh through us, as the Psalms declare: [[quote >> Bible:Psalms 118:22 >> A stone which the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone]]. Having descended to earth through the Father's favor, He united the two peoples—both Jew and Gentile—just as a cornerstone binds two walls together. (14) I said to her, 'It shall flow up to this point and will not overflow.' The Ally replied, 'Let the limit of your waves be so commanded.' For the water is held securely as if by iron bars, yet it moves with ease as if following a set order. I argued, and it cannot be disputed, that this occurs without any external force pushing it, even while it is being lashed by great power and strength. He did not allow the waters to be calm or tranquil so that they might proclaim God's power, struggling against the laws of nature by His command and conquering all through His decree. Had the water been peaceful, many would have attributed its order to the natural properties of water; but now, being tossed, scourged, and driven inward, yet unable to breach its boundaries, it proclaims the might of God through its very turbulence. (Ch. 28, 27) What provided food for the raven? It is said that they do not nurture their young, yet the adults, being large, do provide sustenance in their own way. But who truly nourishes the offspring? Is it not the Word of God? As the Gospel states: [[quote >> Bible:Matthew 6:26 >> Look at the birds of the air; they do not sow or reap, yet your heavenly Father feeds them]]. (Ch. 28, 27) By whose command is the eagle lifted high? And how does the vulture, having settled upon a carcass, cry out from a high rock in secret? ...If there is any rational wisdom in carnivores, it is found in the natural knowledge present in each, directed toward the knowledge of the one I call the dead, even as one carries a vulture. (Ch. 24) Why am I still being judged, being admonished and rebuked by the Lord while I am nothing? Why does he ask why he is being judged for his future? From the beginning, he withdrew from primary things. He says he is defeated by you in matters of justice; why do you advance your judgment so boldly? For what answer is possible? How can one face such a master? He says he was continuing to seek the cause of the plague that befell him, but he summoned no one regarding the creation, and he has nothing to say in response to what has been spoken. —He departs, as if not even rebuking the Lord, being admonished, the wretched man. (Ch. 4, 4) To live as a man by your strength—I will ask you, and you shall answer me. For those who hold rights and do not flee from adversaries, victory comes through their possession. He then defends himself, claiming that men do not concern him; it is clear from that context why this temptation came upon you. I grant you boldness: I will ask, and you shall answer. (Ch. 3) He believes I have used you for any purpose other than to demonstrate your justice. He says the present matter is for profit; he claims he does not speak to condemn, but to prove him just. Or, regarding the temptation, he calls forgiveness a profit, suggesting he was commanded to do this so that he might become something else; he did not say it was so he might change, but so that you might reveal what you truly are and instruct others. See then: he did not say he might become just (for which justice is required...)

choices.choice: The rewrite shifts from the literal, often fragmented 'Pass A' gloss into a cohesive, flowing narrative. It replaces the staccato 'Who is the one who...' with more natural English constructions like 'Who is it that...' and transforms the repetitive 'He says' into integrated dialogue and attribution, moving from a word-for-word translation to a literary interpretation of Origen's rhetorical style.
